quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that the shared center lane is for left turns only. Drivers from both directions can use it to turn left. Do not use this lane for regular driving.

questions.question: Which of these substances can impair your driving and lead to arrest for driving under the influence (DUII)?

options.text: Controlled substances, such as illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants, such as glue or paint

questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription and over-the-counter medicines.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians at all times.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that a steep hill is coming. Adjust your speed to drive safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign means pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to stop and avoid a crash.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: Only for passengers on long drives.
Only for everyone on a highway.
For all occupants every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: For all occupants every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person can become a flying object in a crash and harm others.

questions.question: What color are highway exit distance signs?
questions.explanation: Destination and direction signs are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Make every effort to give them a clear path.
Signal to them when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make every effort to give them a clear path.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, create a clear path for it. If safe, pull to the side of the road to let it pass.

questions.question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles have:
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in mirrors.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always make a complete stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. You must slow down as you approach the intersection and let any vehicles or pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming. Get ready to make a complete stop.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can pass. Drivers in both directions must stay in their lane.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Always signal your turn, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: Turn on your signal at least ____ before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 200 feet before turning or changing lanes. At speeds above 50 mph, signal at least 300 feet before turning.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into separate lanes going each direction. Stay in your lane on the right.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle if possible and move it out of traffic. Check for injuries and call 911. Report the crash to police if anyone is hurt, killed, or if damage is more than $1,000 (or more than $200 to government property like signs).

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: Not needed if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop immediately and move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding but do not move injured people unless necessary. Wait for emergency workers to arrive.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while under the influence of alcohol is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or taking other drugs. It puts both you and others on the road at risk.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This lets you stay in control, keep your car in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic light is coming up.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot park here at any time.

questions.question: What is the only way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your body.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgement?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgement.
It harms both driving skills and judgement.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgement.
It has no effect on judgement but it harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgement.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also affects your judgment of speed and distance, makes you take more risks, and lowers your inhibitions.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the light like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Stop completely, just like you would at a stop sign.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: Directed to do so by a flagger.
It is controlled by a stop sign.
Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger tells you to stop, if there is a stop sign, or if flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey first?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions are more important than signs, signals, or road markings. Police officers, fire police, work zone flag persons, and school crossing guards can all direct traffic.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel at exactly the speed shown.
The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must go this speed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the fastest speed you can legally drive on that road. When it rains, snows, ices, or in other bad conditions, you must drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: When turning right at a red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and let pedestrians and cross traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and let pedestrians and cross traffic go first.
questions.explanation: At a red light, you must stop fully before turning right. Check for pedestrians and other vehicles in your path. Make sure there is no sign that forbids the turn.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol while taking drugs can:

options.text: Make the drugs and alcohol less strong.
Make both the drugs and alcohol stronger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make both the drugs and alcohol stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make both stronger and more dangerous. You should not drive after using either one. Driving after both is even more dangerous.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: The fastest and slowest legal speeds allowed
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest and slowest legal speeds allowed
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the fastest and slowest speeds you can legally drive on a road. The maximum speeds are for good conditions. You must slow down when conditions are bad.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted on roads:
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show where you must stop.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving too slow, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid crashes.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for road conditions

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the shoulder ahead is lower than the road.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of the driver's way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and move away from them. Trying to get back at the driver will make things more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves in the direction the arrow points. In this case, the road curves left. You may see several of these signs along a curve.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel during a traffic stop. Tell any passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is going the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead. Be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving ability?

options.text: The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.explanation: Fatigue affects driving safety the same way alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours impairs you about as much as having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours impairs you about as much as having a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: If you take an over-the-counter drug, you should:

options.text: Keep driving no matter what the label says.

questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. This includes cold and allergy medicine. Check the label for warnings about driving. If you are not sure, ask your doctor or pharmacist before you drive.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
Drivers always checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive within speed limits and slow down when conditions are bad.
